title: Azure Service Bus Overview
description: Understand what Azure Service Bus is, its core concepts, and when to use it for reliable messaging.

data.text: Azure Service Bus is a fully managed messaging service that helps decouple applications and services. It acts as a broker between senders and receivers, ensuring messages are delivered reliably even when services are temporarily offline.

terms.definition: A container for Service Bus messaging entities like queues and topics.
A FIFO (first-in, first-out) buffer where messages wait until a receiver reads them.
A messaging channel that can have multiple subscribers, each receiving a copy of each message.
A named virtual queue within a topic that receives copies of messages matching filters.

data.title: Common Service Bus Patterns
items: Competing Consumers: Multiple receivers read from one queue, processing messages in parallel.
Publish/Subscribe: One sender publishes to a topic, and multiple subscribers receive messages.
Request/Reply: A sender waits for a response on a reply queue or session.
Sessions: Group related messages so they are processed in order by the same receiver.

data.title: Create a Service Bus Namespace (Azure CLI)
data.content: Create a namespace to hold your messaging entities:
data.code:
az servicebus namespace create \
  --resource-group myResourceGroup \
  --name myNamespace \
  --location eastus \
  --sku Basic

cards.title: Queue
cards.description: Point-to-point messaging where one receiver processes each message.
cons: Requires separate queues for different message types

cards.title: Topic + Subscriptions
cards.description: Publish-subscribe where multiple subscribers receive copies of each message.

data.title: Identify the Right Pattern
data.description: For each scenario, decide whether a queue or topic is the better choice.
steps: An e-commerce app needs to process payment requests one at a time in order.
A new user signup event should notify the email service, SMS service, and analytics service.
A background job system needs to distribute image-processing tasks to multiple workers.
A shipping service should receive every order event, and the billing service should also receive every order event.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Service Bus is a managed broker for reliable messaging.
Queues deliver messages to a single consumer in order.
Topics with subscriptions allow many consumers.
Namespaces organize all Service Bus entities.
data.takeaway: Next, you will learn how to create and use Service Bus queues.
